extracted.intended_audience: public company management, in-house counsel, corporate secretaries, and compliance officers responsible for SEC reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for U.S. reporting companies on when and how to prepare and file Form 8-K with the SEC, listing reportable events (Items), required disclosures and exhibits, timing rules, exceptions, and consequences of non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K filing obligation and general timing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 8-K is a current report filed by a U.S. reporting company with the SEC to disclose recent material events or transactions; as a general rule, the Form 8-K must be filed with the SEC within four business days after the occurrence of the reportable event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain events/transactions specified in Form 8-K items trigger the requirement. Companies may also voluntarily furnish information. Timing exceptions (see separate entry) apply. Failure to timely file may result in liability under antifraud provisions and affect Form S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1.01 — Entry Into a Material Definitive Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: File if the registrant has entered into a material definitive agreement not in the ordinary course of business, or any material amendment to such agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'material definitive agreement' provides obligations or rights material to the company. Examples: merger agreements, stock purchase agreements, asset purchase agreements, credit agreements, trust indentures. Non-binding term sheets/LOIs are not definitive. Companies are encouraged (but not required) to attach the agreement as an exhibit; if not attached, the agreement must be filed with the next periodic report. Disclose date entered/amended, parties' identities, and a brief description of material terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1.02 — Termination of a Material Definitive Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: File if a material definitive agreement is terminated and the termination is material to the company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination that occurs on its stated date or due to completion of obligations does not trigger reporting. If termination occurs via advance notice under the agreement, notice triggers filing. Disclose date of termination, parties, brief description of material terms/circumstances surrounding termination, and any material early termination penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1.03 — Bankruptcy or Receivership
rubrics_metrics.description: File if the company becomes the subject of a bankruptcy or receivership court filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose the name/identification of the proceeding, identity of the court, date jurisdiction was assumed, identity of receiver/fiscal agent/similar officer and appointment date. If a plan of reorganization or liquidation is confirmed, describe material features and file/attach the confirmed plan as an exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1.04 — Mine Safety (Shutdowns and Patterns of Violations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators of coal or other mines must file if they receive an imminent danger order under section 107(a) of the Federal Mine Safety and Health Act, or certain written notices from MSHA about patterns of violations or potential for such pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose date of receipt, category of order/notice, and the name and location of the mine involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.01 — Completion of Acquisition or Disposition of Assets
rubrics_metrics.description: File when the company acquires or disposes of a significant amount of assets other than in the ordinary course of business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant if (i) equity in net book value or amount paid/received exceeds 10% of total assets of company and consolidated subsidiaries, or (ii) involves a business that would be a significant business/subsidiary under Rule 11-01 of Regulation S-X. Disclose transaction date, brief description, identity of counterparty, and nature/amount of consideration. File financial statements/pro forma and plans of acquisition/disposition as exhibits under Item 9.01 within required deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.02 — Results of Operations and Financial Condition
rubrics_metrics.description: File when a company publicly announces or releases material, nonpublic information about its results of operations or financial condition for a completed quarterly or annual period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include date of announcement, brief identification, and text of the announcement as an exhibit (commonly an earnings press release). Materials under Item 2.02 are generally 'furnished' rather than 'filed' unless the company states otherwise — the distinction affects liability under Section 18 of the Exchange Act. Other antifraud provisions (e.g., Rule 10b-5) may still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.03 — Creation of a Direct Financial Obligation or Off-Balance Sheet Arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: File if the company becomes obligated on a direct financial obligation or incurs a material obligation arising from an off-balance sheet arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct financial obligations include long-term debt, finance leases, operating leases, and certain short-term obligations outside ordinary course. Disclose date obligated, brief transaction description, amount of obligation, payment terms, material acceleration/increase terms and other material terms. For off-balance sheet obligations, disclose date of becoming directly or contingently liable, material terms, and maximum potential future payments. No duty to disclose until agreement is enforceable against the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.04 — Triggering Events That Accelerate or Increase a Financial Obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: File if a triggering event causes acceleration or increase of a financial obligation and the consequences are material to the company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggering events include event of default, event of acceleration, or similar events. Disclose date/description of triggering agreement, brief description of underlying agreement, increase in obligation amount, payment/acceleration terms, and other material obligations that may arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.05 — Costs Associated With Exit or Disposal Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: File to disclose material write-offs or restructuring charges related to exit or disposal activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include estimates of dollar amounts of (i) each major cost, (ii) total costs, and (iii) cash expenditures. The estimate portion can be delayed until four business days after estimates are known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.06 — Material Impairments
rubrics_metrics.description: File if the company takes a material impairment charge to one or more assets (including securities or goodwill).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report date the board/committee/officers concluded the charge was required, surrounding facts/circumstances, description of impaired assets, and estimates or range of impairment amount. If determination occurs near fiscal quarter/year-end, disclosure may be made in the corresponding Form 10-Q or 10-K instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 3.01 — Notice of Delisting or Failure to Satisfy Continued Listing Rule; Transfer of Listing
rubrics_metrics.description: File when the company receives a notice from its exchange of non-compliance with listing rules, notifies the exchange of material noncompliance, receives a public reprimand from the exchange, or voluntarily withdraws/terminates its listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A company that receives a notice of delisting generally files two Forms 8-K: upon receipt of the first notice and again when delisting is effective. No filing is required if delisting results from conversion or redemption of a security. Filing date is calculated from receipt of the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 3.02 — Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities
rubrics_metrics.description: File if private sales of equity securities exceed thresholds: 1% of outstanding shares of that class (or 5% for smaller reporting companies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose date of sale, title and amount of securities sold, aggregate offering price and commission for cash sales, nature/amount of non-cash consideration, the exemption rule/law relied upon and facts for exemption, and terms of conversion/exercise for convertible/exchangeable securities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 3.03 — Material Modification to Rights of Security Holders
rubrics_metrics.description: File for any material changes to instruments defining holders' rights or material limitations on holders' rights resulting from issuance/modification of another class of securities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose date of modification, title of class involved, and brief description of the modification's effect on holders' rights. Include working capital restrictions and other limitations on dividend payments under this item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 4.01 — Changes in Registrant's Certifying Accountant
rubrics_metrics.description: File if auditors resign, are dismissed, decline reappointment, or the company engages a new auditor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departures and new engagements may require separate Forms 8-K. When auditors leave, disclose whether they were dismissed or resigned, whether departure was board-approved, whether they issued adverse/qualified opinions in past two years, and whether disagreements occurred with financial personnel. When engaging new auditors, disclose name, hire date, and whether the company consulted them prior to engagement. Obligations under this item cannot be avoided by reporting in Form 10-K or 10-Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 4.02 — Non-reliance on Previously Issued Financial Statements or Related Audit Report
rubrics_metrics.description: File if management or an auditor concludes previously issued financial statements should not be relied upon, or if the independent accountant withdraws a previously issued audit report or informs the company it may not rely on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This filing obligation cannot be avoided by reporting the matter in a Form 10-K or 10-Q. Special faster deadlines may apply (see Filing Requirements entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.01 — Changes in Control of Registrant
rubrics_metrics.description: File when the board/committee/authorized officers become aware that a change in control has occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the acquirer, date and description of the transaction causing the change in control, amount of consideration, percentage of voting securities beneficially owned by new control group, and any arrangements between old and new control groups regarding directors or other matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.02 — Departure/Election/Appointment of Directors or Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: File for director resignations/refusal to stand for reelection due to disagreement, election/appointment of new directors outside annual/special meetings, departure of any director, retirement/resignation/termination/demotion of Senior Executive Officers, appointment of Senior Executive Officers, and entry into or amendment of compensatory arrangements with principal officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a company decides not to nominate a director for reelection but the director later resigns, reporting may be triggered. Departures/appointments at subsidiaries do not trigger this item. Include details about the officer/director and material terms of compensatory arrangements as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.03 — Amendments to Articles of Incorporation or Bylaws; Change in Fiscal Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally required to disclose any amendment to articles of incorporation or bylaws or changes in fiscal year unless previously disclosed in a proxy/information statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies that only issue debt securities are typically not required to comply. Restatements without substantive amendments do not require an Item 5.03 filing, but companies are recommended to refile complete restated articles in the next periodic report for investor reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.04 — Temporary Suspension of Trading under Employee Benefit Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: File if there is a prohibition on trading the company's securities under one of its employee benefit plans (blackout period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the reason and length of the blackout period, the securities subject to and transactions suspended, and contact information for a designated person to respond to questions. Filing is required if company receives notice of blackout from plan administrator or if company notifies directors/officers of blackout in absence of such notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.05 — Amendments to Code of Ethics or Waiver for Senior Executive Officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Report amendments to codes of ethics that apply to Senior Executive Officers and any waiver of such provisions for a Senior Executive Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No Form 8-K is needed if the company stated in its most recent annual report/Form 10-K that such amendments/waivers would be disclosed on the company's website and provided the URL. Technical, administrative, or other non-substantive amendments need not be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.06 — Change in Shell Company Status
rubrics_metrics.description: If a shell company completes a transaction that causes it to no longer be a shell company, it must file a Form 8-K describing the material terms of the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies created solely to complete business combinations (e.g., SPACs) are not required to comply with this item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.07 — Submission of Matters to a Vote of Security Holders
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the results of shareholder votes on director elections and all other matters put to a vote within four business days of the end of an annual or special meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final voting results are not available by the Form 8-K due date, the company must file preliminary results and amend the Form 8-K within four days after final results are determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.08 — Shareholder Director Nominations (Schedule 14N notice date)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the company did not hold an annual meeting the prior year, or if this year's meeting date has changed by more than 30 calendar days from the previous year, disclose the date by which a nominating shareholder must submit notice on Schedule 14N of director nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure ensures shareholders know the nomination submission deadline in those circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 6 (Items 6.01–6.06) — Asset-Backed Securities Reporting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers of asset-backed securities must report specified events related to those securities under Items 6.01–6.06.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes ABS informational and computational material (Item 6.01), change of servicer or trustee (6.02), change in credit enhancement or other external support (6.03), failure to make a required distribution (6.04), Securities Act updating disclosure (6.05), and static pool (6.06). Follow Item 1101 of Regulation AB and applicable definitions and exhibit rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 7.01 — Regulation FD Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies may submit a Form 8-K under Item 7.01 to comply with Regulation FD's public disclosure requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information provided under Item 7.01 is generally 'furnished' rather than 'filed' (see Item 2.02 distinction). Regulation FD timing rules also may require simultaneous or next trading day disclosure (see Filing Requirements entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 8.01 — Other Events (voluntary/discretionary disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a company deems an event important to securityholders but not falling under other items, it may disclose the event under Item 8.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly used to report new products, press releases, updates to shelf registration, and other miscellaneous matters. Unlike most Form 8-K filings, Item 8.01 disclosures have no four-business-day filing requirement (voluntary disclosures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 9.01 — Financial Statements and Exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Item 9.01 to file certain financial statements and to list exhibits appended to the Form 8-K (e.g., material definitive agreements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibits referenced under other items (e.g., Item 1.01 agreements, financial statements for acquisitions under Item 2.01) should be appended and cross-referenced here. Special deadlines for filing financial statements of an acquired business apply (see Filing Requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing Form 8-K — combining items, exhibits and cover page boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: A single Form 8-K may include multiple items and may cross-reference exhibits; the cover page permits checking boxes to indicate the Form 8-K satisfies other specified filing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common combinations: unregistered offerings (Items 1.01 & 3.02), acquisitions (Items 1.01 & 2.01), changes to securities (Items 3.03 & 5.03), officer appointments (Items 1.01 & 5.02(c)), director additions (Items 5.02(d) & 5.03). Cover-page boxes include: written communications pursuant to Rule 425 (check first box), soliciting material under Rule 14a-12 (second box), pre-commencement communications under Rules 14d-2(b) or 13e-4(c) (third/fourth boxes). Example: shareholder letters in a business combination may be filed as exhibits under Rule 425.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements and timing exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exceptions, Form 8-K must generally be filed within four business days of the triggering event; several specific exceptions and special deadlines apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable exceptions: Regulation FD filings must be simultaneous with intentional public release or the next trading day for unintentional releases; Item 8.01 voluntary disclosures have no deadline; filing of earnings press releases (Item 2.02) must be completed before any associated analyst conference call; permissible to delay filing related to announcement of new officers until another public announcement (e.g., press release); filing related to auditor's restatement letter (Item 4.02) must be completed within two business days; financial statements of an acquired business (Item 9.01) must be filed no later than 71 calendar days after the initial Form 8-K filing date (four business days plus 71 calendar days). If triggering event occurs on a weekend/holiday, the four-business-day period begins on the first subsequent business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties, shelf eligibility, and interactions with other laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely or properly file may result in severe penalties, including loss of right to use Form S-3 and potential findings regarding disclosure controls under Sarbanes-Oxley; some failures are not deemed violations of Section 10/Rule 10b-5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file may affect eligibility to use Form S-3, delaying access to capital markets. The guidance notes that failure to file under certain items will not affect an issuer's right to use Form S-3 (exceptions listed) and that no failure to file under listed items shall be deemed a violation of Section 10 and Rule 10b-5: Items 1.01, 1.02, 2.03–2.06, 4.02(a), 5.02(e) or 6.03. SEC guidance also treats failure to properly file as prima facie evidence of inadequate disclosure controls under Sarbanes-Oxley. Senior Executive Officers are not required to provide a certification regarding Form 8-K accuracy, even if it includes financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-filing checklist / key disclosure quality questions
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of practical questions companies should consider before preparing/submitting a Form 8-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist items include: Has the company experienced a material event that is reportable under Form 8-K? Have material terms/circumstances been set forth fully and accurately? Is the company 'filing' or 'furnishing' the information? Are all required exhibits attached (and are there other helpful exhibits)? What is the filing deadline and does any special deadline apply? Has the company provided enough information for shareholders to make an informed investment decision? Can the obligation be satisfied in the company's next Form 10-Q or 10-K? Is there confidential information that should be redacted prior to filing?
